long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in a modest Lyon household by Italian immigrant parents, Ricci trained as an engineer in Rome. At Renault Automation he developed systems that allowed machines to communicate, but the company could not staff the resulting client demand. He responded by hiring nine engineers and creating Hysys in 1984. Ricci added three specialist consultancies, combined them as AKKA Technologies and expanded through organic growth and acquisitions into an international engineering and research-and-development group.

The sale of the Ricci family's AKKA holdings to Adecco in 2022 closed that chapter but not his entrepreneurial work. Ricci co-founded INOCEL with explorer Mike Horn to commercialise high-power hydrogen fuel cells, serving as investor and chair of its strategic committee while professional executives run the company. Alongside his brother Jean-Franck, he also took ownership of Bertone and has supported its return as a limited-production coachbuilder through the GB110 hypercar and Runabout.

uncertainties.detail: The source record and early French corporate documents use Maurice Ricci; later AKKA, Adecco, INOCEL and Bertone materials use Mauro Ricci. AKKA's own report explicitly introduces Mauro and then states that Maurice Ricci founded Hysys, while exact birth and career records align. Mauro is treated as the established professional alias, not a separate person, and the source display name remains unchanged.

The input records French nationality and France birth country. UK and French corporate records identify the same Lyon-born executive as Italian, consistent with reporting that his parents emigrated from Italy. The dossier preserves French as the primary source value and proposes Italian only as a secondary nationality; it does not infer citizenship history or timing.

INOCEL is Ricci's clearest current public founder-investor role and supports Energy as primary industry. He also co-owns the active Bertone automotive marque and holds investment structures, so Energy is not presented as his only present interest or as a complete portfolio valuation.

Adecco's disclosures establish acquisition of Ricci-family holdings and a mix of cash and Adecco shares. They do not separate every family member's beneficial proceeds in the public summary. The dossier therefore uses the transaction to establish monetisation of the founder-built asset without assigning the overall deal value or all family consideration to Maurice personally.

Le Progrès describes a modest household, identifies both parents' non-owner occupations and documents Ricci's employee-to-founder transition. This supports Self-made — independent start. It does not prove that he received no ordinary family support, which the classification does not require.

The LinkedIn account is verified through the unique Hysys-AKKA-INOCEL chronology and first-person Adecco transaction post. No separate identity-verified active personal Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website met the publication threshold; namesake accounts were excluded.

Mediapart's direct Maoro-company evidence is used only to resolve person ID 1817. The biographies, classifications and tags exclude the asset's name, specifications, ownership structure, tax treatment and leisure use.
